subject: How do I return the data that falls within a bin (i.e. from stat_bin or geom_histogram)?

messages.author: fbe8141cf257d21e
messages.subject: How do I return the data that falls within a bin (i.e. from stat_bin or geom_histogram)?
parts:
Ultimately, I would like to take all the data that falls within a bin (i.e. of a histogram), and I would like to apply other functions to that data so that I can plot other things on the y-axis (instead of plotting just the counts on the y-axis). So for example, here is a sample of my data:

>head(poolSingSumm)
  CHR   POS REF Alt TsTv N_RefReads N_AltReads         Frq
1  2L  5495   A   T   Tv       1439         13 0.008953168
2  2L  9037   C   T   Ts       1888         14 0.007360673
3  2L 11255   A   T   Tv       1018         38 0.035984848
4  2L 25344   T   A   Tv        855         34 0.038245219
5  2L 25665   A   T   Tv        776         31 0.038413879
6  2L 25940   G   T   Tv        970          8 0.008179959

And if I do this:
>ggplot(poolSingSumm,aes(x=Frq,y=..density..,fill=TsTv)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=0.005)

This gives me a histogram where each bin has a height for the total counts, but is also colored so that it shows me the proportion of the data that is categorized as Ts or Tv within that bin. 

What I want is the data within that bin, so that I can do other things to it. I figure this must exist somewhere, since it is being used do the fill in the histogram. I tried to use stat_bin but it is not well documented what stat_bin is returning. Is there a ggplot function I can use to access my binned data?

Thanks!
Zoe

messages.author: 6ed2ff7838c0c40e
messages.subject: Re: How do I return the data that falls within a bin (i.e. from stat_bin or geom_histogram)?
parts:
The data for the plot can be extracted, but it might be easier to pre-summarise the data yourself. Here are examples of both methods, using the built-in mtcars data frame for illustration:

library(gridExtra) # For grid.arrange function
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # For summarizing data

Method 1: Use ggplot_build to extract data from plot object.

# Create a plot similar to yours
p1 = ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=mpg, y=..density.., fill=factor(cyl))) + geom_histogram(binwidth=5)

# Extract data using function ggplot_build
p1build = ggplot_build(p1)
plotData = p1build$data[[1]]

Where plotData is a data frame containing the data that ggplot created to build the histogram. One more thing: I don't think you need "y=..density..".

Method 2: Pre-summarize the data

# Pre-summarize the data
mpgBins = mtcars %>% group_by(cyl, mpgCut=cut(mpg, seq(0,40,5))) %>%
  summarise(count=n())

You can also, of course, plot the pre-summarized data:

p2 = ggplot(mpgBins, aes(mpgCut, count, fill=factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity")

# Compare the two plots
grid.arrange(p1,p2)

If you want to add the categorical bins to your original data set, rather than just have a summary version, you can use the cut function for that as well:

mtcars = mtcars %>%
                  mutate(mpgBins = cut(mpg, seq(0, 40, 5)))

or, in base R

mtcars$mpgBins = cut(mtcars$mpgBins, seq(0, 40, 5))

Hope that helps.

Joel
